Description

Noxious stimulation of the joint releases substance P from the central terminals of peptidergic afferents in the superficial dorsal horn. Substance P binds the neurokinin 1 receptor on lamina I projection neurons, which signals through Gq and phospholipase Cβ and is then internalised. Lamina I neurons carrying this receptor are needed for hyperalgesia.

Colour

Each block is coloured by its effect on pain, red where it raises pain and blue where it relieves it, and everything in it takes that colour, GTP and GDP included, as it works for the block's result. Drugs are yellow and classes of molecules white.

This block is red: substance P carries and amplifies nociceptive signals.
